Syscalls for BN128, Poseidon, and secp256k1 crypto operations in the VM.

# Purpose
This file implements Solana VM syscall handlers for cryptographic operations. It provides entry points for `alt_bn128` group operations, `alt_bn128` point compression and decompression, Poseidon hashing, and `secp256k1` public key recovery. Each function reads input data from VM memory, checks syscall arguments, updates compute unit cost with the matching cost model, translates output memory, and writes the result back to the caller. The code follows the syscall behavior used by Agave and returns Solana-style error codes through `*_ret`.

The main technical parts are the wrappers around the crypto primitives in `fd_bn254`, `fd_poseidon`, and `fd_secp256k1`. The [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_alt_bn128_group_op`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_alt_bn128_group_op>) and [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_alt_bn128_compression`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_alt_bn128_compression>) functions handle BN254 curve arithmetic and point format conversion. The [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_poseidon`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_poseidon>) function validates parameters, maps a list of input slices, and computes a Poseidon hash with the requested endianness. The [`fd_vm_syscall_sol_secp256k1_recover`](<#fd_vm_syscall_sol_secp256k1_recover>) function validates the recovery ID, recovers the public key from the hash and signature, and stores the 64-byte result in VM memory.
